question: NATO, the US and the EU are constantly receiving reports about the ‘unexpected’ fate of weapons sent to Ukraine. Modern anti-tank systems, grenade launchers, small arms, expensive artillery systems, missile systems and high-tech recognition equipment are unaccounted for.

Former whistle-blowers from the Ukrainian Ministry of Defence report that they have been able to identify NATO weapons that are being resold by the Ukrainian Government. It is said that European weapons intended for Ukraine are being sold on the darknet by anonymous groups using the ‘stash’ method: the buyer pays using bitcoin or other cryptocurrencies and is then informed by the seller where the weapons are hidden.

These weapons often follow the routes of Ukrainian grain... In the worst cases, they end up on the black market and ultimately in international war hotspots and in the hands of terrorist organisations and drug cartels. European taxpayers deserve to know what is becoming of the exorbitant profits obtained in an underhand way using their money. In view of this, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Is the Commission demanding information from the Ukrainian Government regarding the number of weapons supplied by the EU that have been destroyed and the number that have ‘gone missing’ in Ukraine? How often is the Commission receiving this kind of information?

In view of the large number of cases reported, how does the Commission intend to investigate the suspected profits made by members of the Ukrainian Government from the trafficking of arms obtained through European aid?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.10.2024) Since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale aggression of Ukraine, the EU and its Member States have delivered unprecedented levels of military financial support for the Ukrainian armed forces, notably via the European Peace Facility (EPF). 1.

For any assistance measures benefiting the Armed Forces of Ukraine through the EPF, the Government of Ukraine has committed to ensure compliance with the requirements and conditions established by the Council1. Thereby, the Ukrainian authorities took the commitment neither to transfer the equipment received under the EPF to any third parties outside its own armed forces, nor to re-export it to other countries.

They also committed to ensure safe and secure maintenance and management of weapons and ammunition delivered under the EPF. The European External Action Service is responsible for monitoring and evaluating the implementation of these commitments with the beneficiary and has carried out on-site inspections in Ukraine to verify the adequate storage, management and accounting of EPF-donated equipment.

During the on-site checks, no irregularities or infringements of these commitments have been identified. 2. Jointly with Member States and Ukraine, the EU has implemented a list of actions to counter potential trafficking of firearms, other small arms and light weapons in the context of Russia’s war of aggression since 2023. To date, there is no evidence that any EPF equipment donated to Ukraine has been diverted.

In case of violations of the arrangements between the High Representative/Vice-President (HR/VP) and the Government of Ukraine deriving from the Council Decision 2021/509, the EU’s Political and Security Committee (PSC) may decide to suspend (wholly or partially) the implementation of an assistance measure.

In urgent and exceptional cases, the HR/VP may provisionally suspend wholly or partially the implementation of an assistance measure, pending a decision by the PSC. The PSC may also recommend to the Council the termination of an assistance measure.
